nodes.name: Carl Cox
nodes.description: British DJ and producer who came up through the late-1980s rave circuit and built his sets on hard techno and house. Held a long summer residency at Space Ibiza and founded the Intec label.

nodes.name: Laurent Garnier
nodes.description: French DJ and producer who started DJing in Manchester in the late 1980s before returning to France. Recorded several techno albums and co-founded the F Communications label.

nodes.name: David Guetta
nodes.description: Paris club DJ turned producer whose 2009 album One Love paired house production with pop and R&B vocalists. Topped the DJ Mag Top 100 poll several times.

nodes.name: Calvin Harris
nodes.description: Scottish DJ, producer and songwriter who sang on his own early electro singles such as "Acceptable in the 80s". The 2012 album 18 Months made him an international dance-pop producer.

nodes.name: Tiësto
nodes.description: Dutch DJ and producer who co-founded Black Hole Recordings in 1997 and recorded as Gouryella with Ferry Corsten. Moved from trance mix series to mainstream EDM festival production.

nodes.name: Skrillex
nodes.description: Los Angeles producer who fronted the post-hardcore band From First to Last before going solo. His aggressive dubstep EPs carried bass music into American EDM festivals.

nodes.name: Diplo
nodes.description: American DJ and producer who founded Mad Decent in 2006 and produced M.I.A.'s "Paper Planes". Leads the dancehall-electronic project Major Lazer and formed Jack Ü with Skrillex.

nodes.name: Martin Garrix
nodes.description: Dutch DJ and producer whose 2013 single "Animals" launched him as a teenage festival headliner. Founded the Stmpd Rcrds label in 2016.

nodes.name: Bob Sinclar
nodes.description: Paris producer and DJ behind Yellow Productions, mixing disco samples with house grooves. A key name of the late-1990s French house wave.

nodes.name: Kaytranada
nodes.description: Haitian-Canadian producer and DJ who built a following through mixtapes and remixes before signing to XL Recordings. His album Bubba won the Grammy for Best Dance/Electronic Album.

nodes.name: Peggy Gou
nodes.description: South Korean DJ, producer and singer based in Berlin who released EPs on Ninja Tune and Phonica. Launched Gudu Records in 2019 and released her debut album I Hear You in 2024.

nodes.name: Nina Kraviz
nodes.description: Russian DJ, producer and singer known for raw, hypnotic techno sets and her own vocal productions.

nodes.name: Charlotte de Witte
nodes.description: Belgian DJ and producer of stripped-back acid and minimal techno who first recorded as Raving George. Founded the KNTXT label.

nodes.name: Ben Klock
nodes.description: German techno DJ and producer who became a resident at Berghain in Berlin. Founded the Klockworks label in 2006.

nodes.name: Black Coffee
nodes.description: South African DJ and producer who gained attention through the 2004 Red Bull Music Academy and founded Soulistic Music. His deep, soulful house later won a Grammy for Best Dance/Electronic Album.

nodes.name: Paul Oakenfold
nodes.description: English DJ and producer who brought Balearic club sounds back to London in the late 1980s. Moved into trance and remixed acts from U2 to Madonna.

nodes.name: Sasha
nodes.description: Welsh DJ and producer who started out playing acid house in the late 1980s. His 1990s mix albums with John Digweed shaped progressive house.

nodes.name: John Digweed
nodes.description: British DJ and producer who partnered with Sasha on touring and mix albums and recorded with Nick Muir as Bedrock. Built long-form progressive house sets.

nodes.name: Eric Prydz
nodes.description: Swedish DJ and producer who also records as Pryda and Cirez D. Broke through with "Call on Me" in 2004 and released the album Opus in 2016.

nodes.name: Four Tet
nodes.description: Stage name of English producer Kieran Hebden, who left the post-rock band Fridge for solo electronic work. Blends acoustic samples and club rhythms, and has collaborated with Burial and Madlib.

nodes.name: Fred again..
nodes.description: British producer, songwriter and DJ who wrote and produced for Ed Sheeran and Stormzy. His Actual Life albums build club tracks around found voice recordings.

nodes.name: Moby
nodes.description: American musician who moved from punk bands to DJing, producing and remixing in New York around 1989. His 1991 single "Go" brought rave techno to the charts.

nodes.name: DJ Premier
nodes.description: American DJ and producer who formed Gang Starr with Guru. His chopped jazz and soul samples and scratched hooks defined much of 1990s New York rap production.

nodes.name: Pete Rock
nodes.description: American producer, DJ and rapper who rose with Pete Rock & CL Smooth in the early 1990s. Known for layered horn and jazz samples and his remix work.

nodes.name: J Dilla
nodes.description: Detroit producer, rapper and composer who emerged with Slum Village and co-founded the Soulquarians. His loose, off-grid drum programming shaped hip-hop and neo-soul, and his last album Donuts was released days before his death.

nodes.name: Madlib
nodes.description: American DJ, producer and rapper from Oxnard, California, known for dense, sample-based production. Recorded as Madvillain with MF Doom and as Jaylib with J Dilla.

nodes.name: Marley Marl
nodes.description: Queensbridge DJ and producer whose sampled drum breaks helped define early New York rap production. Producers including DJ Premier, Pete Rock and Madlib cite him as an influence.

nodes.name: Justice
nodes.description: Paris electronic duo of Gaspard Augé and Xavier de Rosnay, mixing distorted electro-house with rock and disco. Their debut album Cross appeared in 2007.

nodes.name: Disclosure

nodes.name: Jamie xx
